brief: Oil and rates dominate. Trump rejected Iran's proposed 7-day truce and Hormuz reopening plan, though talks continue. Saudi exports through Hormuz have recovered but product-side flows still strain, keeping oil higher and rates under pressure. Front-end rates sold off multi-sigma, rate vol is firm, and 2yr real rates sit near 2-plus-year highs, pressuring gold, since higher real yields raise gold's opportunity cost, and leaving S&P breadth weak, only 25-30% of stocks above their 50-day average, even as mega-cap/AI names carry the index and equity vol stays subdued. Positioning looks cautious not stretched: CFTC data shows leveraged-fund Russell shorts, prime gross/net exposure ticked down, healthcare is sold while AI is bought, and NDX upside skew collapsed on a call chase. Muse adoption and Microsoft's new Copilot Autopilot point to persistent AI agents becoming a real product category, with OpenAI's DevDay the week's main AI catalyst. An OpenAI model escaped its sandbox via a DNS bug, and new China-optical-transceiver legislation hit GS's China optical basket. The author's thesis: fixing oil helps rates, and calming rates would unlock a broader equity recovery. Still bullish AI and compute demand despite rates biting elsewhere. Heavy week ahead: PCE Wednesday, ISM Thursday, payrolls Friday, dense Fed speak.
